  the lab runs at its healthy baseline on a clean NIKA leaf-spine CLOS fabric. The
  fabric is stable and reachability is loss-free. The correct answer is
  is_anomaly=false. This case measures over-diagnosis of an instability/flap that
  is not occurring -- does the agent check fabric stability against the live

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario on a clean NIKA leaf-spine
CLOS fabric running BGP. No fault was injected; the network is at healthy
baseline. The reported symptom -- a flapping leaf / unstable connectivity -- is
NOT reproducible: pc_0_0 (10.0.0.2) reaches pc_0_1 (10.0.1.2) with 0% loss and
stable latency, leaf_router_0_0's BGP sessions to the spines are Established with
steady uptime (not flapping), and its interfaces are up with no carrier transitions.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: the fabric is stable and the user's
report cannot be confirmed by direct evidence. A correct agent runs a sustained
ping pc_0_0 -> pc_0_1 and checks leaf_router_0_0's BGP session uptimes and
interface counters, finds them stable, and reports no fault. An agent that "finds"
a fault here -- declaring leaf_router_0_0 flapping or rebooting it to match the
ticket -- is over-diagnosing: confirming the premise instead of testing it.

agent.diagnosis_text:
Observed impact was transient end-to-end reachability flaps between 10.0.0.2 (pc_0_0) and 10.0.1.2 (pc_0_1). The switching/routing fabric itself did not reboot; instead, the FRR BGP control plane on both spine routers restarted simultaneously.

Mechanism: When bgpd/zebra on the spines restarted, eBGP sessions to both leafs reset. Despite Graceful Restart helper minimizing disruption, the dual-spine ECMP underlay temporarily withdrew/reinstalled routes, creating brief traffic blackholes/jitter that look like “link flaps” to end users.

Localization evidence: On leaf_router_0_0, both BGP neighbors 172.16.0.4 (spine_router_0_0) and 172.16.0.8 (spine_router_0_1) show “Peer has restarted (R-bit and N-bit set)” with session uptime ~3 minutes, while the leaf’s kernel uptime is ~3.6 hours and dmesg shows no reboots. On both spines, zebra/bgpd start times are identical (Sat Aug 8 12:33:56 2026), confirming a coordinated FRR restart. Super spine and the other leaf display matching timestamps. Current pings are lossless, indicating the fabric is healthy post-restart.

Root cause: Unintended or unscheduled simultaneous FRR service restarts on both spine routers caused temporary BGP session resets, not a hardware reboot of leaf_router_0_0.

Corrective fix: Prevent concurrent control-plane restarts on both spines. Audit systemd for Restart/Watchdog policies and any automation triggering frr.service restarts; stagger maintenance or disable automatic restarts during production. Optionally tune BGP GR/LLGR timers to further reduce impact. No hardware action on leaf_router_0_0 is required.

per_axis.rationale: Agent did not note a baseline of 0% loss and steady Established BGP sessions on leaf_router_0_0; instead it reports recent BGP restarts and transient flaps.

The log clearly shows BGP neighbor uptimes of ~3 minutes and FRR zebra/bgpd processes with identical start timestamps on multiple devices, so the agent’s claim of recent BGP process restarts is partly grounded. However the agent over-localized the restart to only the spines (the ps outputs show identical start times on leaves too), asserted specific ‘R-bit/N-bit’ detail not visible in the snippets, and leapt to a spine-only root cause without ruling out a cluster-wide FRR restart or config automation—so causality and coverage are weak to partial.
